skill.name: writing-hookify-rules
skill.description: Create and refine Hookify markdown rules that watch Claude events, match patterns, and show warning or blocking messages.
skill.summary: Guides users through Hookify rule syntax, event types, conditions, file placement, and regex patterns.
skill.author: CaptainCrouton89

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples that teach users to detect risky commands, secrets, or eval patterns. I confirmed risk around dynamic command interpolation and global hidden rule placement because generated Hookify rules can execute local commands and apply across projects. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Dynamic command interpolation can execute local commands from hook messages.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger guidance to avoid interpolation by default, require explicit review, and restrict examples to read-only commands.

remediation.issue: Global rules under ~/.claude can affect every project.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend project-scoped rules by default and warn that global rules should be reviewed regularly.

remediation.issue: Dangerous command examples may be misunderstood outside their detection context.
remediation.suggestion: Label destructive command patterns as detection-only examples and avoid exact destructive paths when placeholders are sufficient.

content.user_title: Create Hookify Rules for Claude Workflows
content.value_statement: Hook rules are hard to write correctly because event fields, regex patterns, and messages must align. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Hookify rule structure and practical patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Hookify rule frontmatter fields, including name, enabled, event, action, pattern, and conditions.
Shows simple and multi-condition rule formats for bash, file, stop, prompt, and all events.
Provides regex examples for dangerous commands, debug code, sensitive files, and generated files.
Describes where project and global Hookify rule files should be placed.
Gives naming, gitignore, and escaping guidance for local Hookify rule files.
Documents dynamic command interpolation behavior and timeout notes.
limitations: It does not install Hookify or verify that a local Hookify runtime is configured.
It does not automatically test generated regex patterns against real command logs.
Dynamic command interpolation requires careful review because it can execute local commands.
The examples are templates and may need project-specific field names or patterns.

use_cases.title: Create a Bash Safety Warning
use_cases.description: Draft a Hookify rule that warns before risky shell commands run in a coding session.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guardrails
use_cases.description: Build project-scoped rules that remind agents about tests, logs, generated files, and review steps.

use_cases.title: Review Sensitive File Patterns
use_cases.description: Create rules that detect edits to environment files, credentials, and certificate-like paths.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Bash Warning
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner rule for one command pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule that warns when Claude tries to run [command pattern]. Include the filename and a clear message.

prompt_templates.title: Add a File Edit Guardrail
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate rule for one file edit pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify rule that watches file edits for [pattern] in [file type]. Explain each frontmatter field.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Condition Rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify rule with conditions for file_path matching [path pattern] and new_text containing [text]. Use action [warn or block].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Rule Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design across event types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three Hookify rules for [workflow]. Include bash, file, and stop events, with concise messages and regex notes.

output_examples.input: Warn when Claude adds console logging to TypeScript files.
output_examples.output: A project Hookify rule named warn-console-log that watches file edits, checks TypeScript paths, and warns with cleanup guidance.
A bash Hookify rule concept that catches recursive removal, disk formatting, and broad permission changes before execution.

output_examples.input: Remind the agent to run tests before stopping.
output_examples.output: A stop event reminder that asks for test, build, and documentation checks before the session ends.

best_practices: Use narrow regex patterns so rules catch real risks without blocking normal work.
Prefer project rules for team-specific behavior and reserve global rules for personal standards.
Review any rule that uses dynamic command interpolation before enabling it.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad patterns that match common words across unrelated commands.
Do not store project-specific rules as global rules unless every project needs them.
Do not include secret values in Hookify messages, examples, or pattern text.

faq.question: What is Hookify?
faq.answer: Hookify uses markdown rules with YAML frontmatter to match Claude events and display warnings or blocks.

faq.question: Which events can this skill help with?
faq.answer: It covers bash, file, stop, prompt, and all events, including simple and conditional matching.

faq.question: Can it create blocking rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft rules that use the block action for supported events when a match occurs.

faq.question: Does it test rules automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest test commands and regex checks, but local validation remains your responsibility.

faq.question: Where should generated rules be stored?
faq.answer: Use project .claude rules for shared work. Use global home rules only for personal rules that should apply everywhere.

faq.question: Is dynamic command interpolation safe?
faq.answer: It can be useful, but it runs local commands. Review commands and outputs before enabling those rules.
